blockingFindings.finding: EP6 validates an EvaluationAuthorityIndexV1 value supplied inside the ordinary serializable EvaluationAuthorityAdmissionInputV1. The declared admit_evaluation_authority constructor has no trusted ProjectStore reader/writer, no opaque store-read result, and no atomic durable insert/read transition. Exactly-one cardinality over a caller-provided list is not store admission. A byte-identical row originating from the caller and a byte-identical row originating from durable trusted storage are observationally indistinguishable to this constructor. Therefore the constructor can mint its module-private AdmittedEvaluationAuthorityV1 from self-attested store state. Private/non-Display/non-Serialize output prevents direct handle forgery but cannot repair untrusted input provenance.

formalIndistinguishabilityProof.acceptedInput: x = the published positive-vector EvaluationAuthorityAdmissionInputV1 including its single EvaluationAuthorityIndexV1 row
formalIndistinguishabilityProof.attackerInput: x' = a caller-created serialization byte-identical to x, including the same index row
formalIndistinguishabilityProof.constructorObservation: admit_evaluation_authority(x) and admit_evaluation_authority(x') receive the same values and bytes; the declared interface exposes no provenance bit, trusted store handle, transaction receipt or opaque store-read capability
formalIndistinguishabilityProof.consequence: Any deterministic implementation conforming only to the declared API must return the same result for x and x'. Since x is accepted, x' earns the opaque capability.

contractDrift: EP6 invariant EP-12 still says RR13-01 admission remains pending coordinated Evidence/OP/store work and names VerifiedEvaluationAuthorityInputV1.

Evidence v5 declares a different split API: opensip_store.admit_evaluation_authority_seal_v1(ProjectStore, ...) -> AdmittedEvaluationAuthoritySealV1 followed by bind_evaluation_authority_v2(...). EP6 does not consume that opaque store result.
blockingFindings.whyDownstreamPassesDoNotCloseIt: RT11 and VERSIONING-v6 exactly preserve the bytes and graph that EP6 declares admitted, but custody of a self-attested admission is not proof of trusted admission. Their mechanical passes are conditional on repairing this root boundary.
requiredRepair: Define a trusted ProjectStore port that atomically inserts or resolves EvaluationAuthorityIndexV1 by the exact (ProjectId, evaluationAuthoritySealRef) key and enforces durable uniqueness/conflict behavior.

Make the store return an opaque module-private AdmittedEvaluationAuthoritySealV1 or equivalent authenticated store-read capability; make the EP6 constructor consume that opaque value, not a row/list supplied by the caller.
Specify and test missing, duplicate, conflicting, collision, transaction-failure and replay/idempotency behavior at the trusted store boundary.
Align EP6's constructor and types with Evidence v5's ProjectStore admission/bind API, and reconcile EP-12 / activationAuthority / authorityAdmissionContract type drift.
Add an adversarial selftest in which a caller provides the exact accepted index bytes without a trusted store capability; it must fail before core invocation.
Regenerate EP6, RT11, VERSIONING-v6, Evidence/OP joins and the response under a new stable hash window, then obtain a fresh independent combined rereview.
